citation.title: Optimisation of three-dimensional hierarchical structures with tailored lattice metamaterial anisotropy
citation.authors: Lei Zhu, Liao Sun, Xiaoyang Wang, Nan Li
citation.venue: Materials & Design 210 (2021) 110083 (Elsevier; available online 2 September 2021; open access, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per the article's first page)
citation.version_coded: Version of record: the typeset publisher PDF (19 pp., journal header and CC BY-NC-ND licence line) deposited in Spiral, Imperial College London's repository (hdl.handle.net/10044/1/92217; OpenAlex labels this copy submittedVersion), read in full as text; pp. 10, 12, 13 and 15 also checked on rendered pages for Figs. 9, 12, 16 and 19

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screening code confirmed at full text)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: MBB beam at volume fraction 0.3: the ANN-surrogate lattice optimization with orthotropic PC cells (PC-A) reaches 30.6% lower compliance than solid-void SIMP (p = 3) and 13.0% lower than quasi-isotropic PC lattices, on the same Nastran platform.
claim.key_phrase: is 30.6% lower than that of the topology optimisation case (Iso-P3)
claim.location: Sec. 6 Conclusions, p. 17 (first quantitative comparison with a classical method; the abstract's comparison is qualitative, §5.1 rule 2); the same values are plotted in Fig. 16, p. 13
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable: no run time of any method is reported. The ANN surrogates are said to improve computational efficiency over direct homogenization (abstract; highlights; Sec. 2.1, 3.3), without numbers.
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract, qualitative: anisotropic lattice designs have better structural efficiency than classical TO and quasi-isotropic lattice optimization. (2) Fig. 12, MBB beam at vf 0.5, compliance normalised by SIMP p = 3: PC-A 0.86, SIMP p = 2 0.86, SIMP p = 1 0.65, PC-Q 0.91, BCC-Q 0.95, BCC-A 0.94, PCBCC-Q 0.98, PCBCC-A 0.87. (3) Fig. 19, L-shaped beam at vf 0.3: PC-A 0.69 vs SIMP p = 3 1.00, SIMP p = 2 0.74, SIMP p = 1 0.43. (4) Fig. 16 and p. 14: the PC-A curve almost coincides with SIMP p = 2 over vf 0.3-0.9, and SIMP p = 1 lies below all lattice designs. (5) Efficiency of the ANN surrogate: asserted, never measured.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP compliance minimization with an isotropic power-law material: penalty 3 (Iso-P3, the solid-void benchmark), plus penalties 1 and 2 (Iso-P1, Iso-P2) as intermediate-density references; same filter, volume constraint and optimizer as the lattice cases (Sec. 5, Table 2)
baseline.implementation: Commercial: Nastran 2018 FE solver with its built-in modified method of feasible directions (MMFD) optimizer, driven by a user-defined MATLAB program (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 4); the lattice data come from an adapted 149-line MATLAB homogenization code (ref. [35], Sec. 3.2)
baseline.problem_size: 3D hexahedral meshes with one element per lattice cell (Sec. 2.2); MBB beam with dimensions 6L, 3L and L, half modelled by symmetry (Fig. 9); L-shaped beam (Fig. 18); cantilever (Fig. 21); element counts not stated. At least 8 lattice cells per dimension are required for scale separation (Sec. 5.1)
baseline.classical_iterations: Stopping on the relative change of the objective and the constraint violation (Sec. 2.1, p. 4); tolerances and iteration counts not stated
baseline.training_time: not stated; one-hidden-layer ANNs with 2-9 neurons per output (Table B1), trained with Levenberg-Marquardt in MATLAB on a 70/15/15 split; R² at least 0.98 (Table 1), RMSE 0.002-0.027 (Table B2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; numerical homogenization of 165 (PC), 330 (BCC) and 1,327 (PCBCC) strut-radius samples, with the rest of the 729, 4,096 and 5,832 full-factorial samples obtained by rotation (Sec. 3.1, p. 5)
baseline.quality_metric: Optimised compliance from the Nastran FE analysis of the homogenised macroscale model (ANN-predicted effective properties for lattice cases, power-law densities for SIMP), normalised by the SIMP p = 3 value (Figs. 12, 16, 19, 22)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB beam, vf 0.3: PC-A 30.6% below SIMP p = 3 and 13.0% below PC-Q (Sec. 6). MBB beam, vf 0.5: PC-A 0.86 vs SIMP p = 3 1.00 (Fig. 12). L-shaped beam, vf 0.3: PC-A 0.69 vs 1.00 (Fig. 19). Against SIMP p = 2 the PC-A values are about equal (0.86 vs 0.86; 0.69 vs 0.74). Achieved volume fractions are not reported

R1.evidence: Sec. 5, Figs. 12, 16 and 19: all designs solve the same compliance problem with the same volume-fraction constraint, mesh, filter, MMFD optimizer and convergence criteria on the same platform, and compliance is compared directly; no speed claim is involved. Caveats: tolerances and achieved volumes are not stated, and the SIMP p = 3 designs keep filter-induced grey regions without post-processing (p. 11). A verifier who weighs these may choose partial (R1-loose).

R2.evidence: No run time is reported for any method; the comparison is compliance only. SIMP and the lattice cases run in the same commercial Nastran MMFD module (Sec. 4), so criteria (a)-(e) do not apply.

R3.evidence: The efficiency gain of the ANN over direct homogenization is asserted (abstract; Sec. 2.1, 3.3) but never measured. For C3: the homogenization of 165, 330 and 1,327 samples (Sec. 3.1) and the ANN training are not costed; no break-even is given.

R4.evidence: Figs. 12, 16 and 19: compliance comes from a Nastran FE analysis of the optimised designs, but of the homogenised model with ANN-predicted properties. The returned lattice CAD model, with radii averaged at strut junctions (p. 14), is not analysed in detail. The homogenization check covers uniform lattices only (Sec. 5.1, Table C1: strain-energy difference below 5% at 8 cells per dimension). Achieved volume fractions and failed runs are not reported. A stricter reading (lattice performance partly surrogate-predicted) gives fail.

reporting.n_test_cases: 3 case studies: MBB beam (9 material cases at vf 0.5, Fig. 12; 5 cases over vf 0.3-0.9, Fig. 16), L-shaped beam (8 cases at vf 0.3, Fig. 19), cantilever torsion (3 lattice cases at vf 0.3, no SIMP case, Fig. 22)

notes: Screening code I-QUALITY confirmed. Primary-outcome judgment: the abstract compares with classical TO only qualitatively, so §5.1 rule 2 selects the conclusion's first quantitative comparison (MBB beam, vf 0.3, 30.6% lower compliance than SIMP p = 3), which matches the Fig. 16 sweep. Attribution caveat [inferred]: the ANN only replaces the homogenization lookup; the compliance gain comes from the lattice design space (intermediate densities with real lattice properties, plus anisotropy), and the ANN's own contribution is not isolated. Against SIMP with p = 2 the PC-A designs are about equal, and SIMP with p = 1 gives lower compliance than every lattice design (Figs. 12, 16, 19); the authors treat p = 1 and p = 2 as physically meaningless (p. 10). The Fig. 12 and Fig. 19 values were read from the printed bar and panel labels on the rendered pages. Internal inconsistencies: the Fig. 11-12 captions cite 'Table 3' for the case list, which is Table 2; the lattice is named PCBCC in most of the text and BCCPC in Fig. 12 and Sec. 5.2; the conclusion attributes the 30.6% to the MBB beam at vf 0.3, while Sec. 5.2 runs vf 0.5 and vf 0.3 appears only in the Fig. 16 sweep; relative density is described as total voxels divided by solid voxels (p. 7), the inverse of Eq. 2. Access: the listed open copy on ScienceDirect answered curl with HTTP 403 and a captcha page; no challenge was attempted, and the Spiral repository copy (listed by OpenAlex) was used. No code or data statement. Duplicate check: no other pool record or prefill of this study. No author named Jun Wang.
